_readme: Voiceover script for locale-driver-training.html — edit the text freely.
Run `python3 narration.py voices` to pick a voice, put its id in voice_id below,
then `python3 narration.py speak` to generate audio/s1.mp3 ... audio/s9.mp3.
Scene durations in the animation follow these clips automatically.

scenes.s1: Every route starts with your DSP. Before your shift, they'll send you a route number. That number is how the warehouse knows which orders are yours, so keep it handy — dispatch is going to ask for it the moment you walk in.
scenes.s2: When you get to the warehouse, head for the roll-up door and find the on-site dispatcher. Pull up the check-in code on your phone, show it to them, and give them your route number.
scenes.s3: Dispatch will pull your rack and wheel it out to you. It's a rolling shelf unit — four shelves, holding around twenty insulated bags. That rack is your entire route.
scenes.s4: Before you take it anywhere, count it. Go shelf by shelf and check every single bag. If something is missing, this is the moment to say so — not after you've already left the warehouse.
scenes.s5: Let dispatch know you're heading out, then load your car with a bit of care. Bags lie flat and stay put. Don't stack orders on top of each other, and don't let them slide around back there. That's how food arrives damaged.
scenes.s6: Now the part that matters most: the label. Look at the bottom-left corner. That's your route number and your stop number — which bag this is, and the order you drop it in. And up in the top-right, you'll see your DSP name on a colored background. Remember that color.
scenes.s7: At the stop, don't guess — read the labels. Find the bag whose route and stop number match where you are. Then check whether it's one bag or several. If two or more are zip-tied together, that's a single multi-bag order. Cut the tie and carry all of them in together. Never split an order.
scenes.s8: Hand the order to the customer and take your delivery photo. Then collect the empties — jars and bags that go back to the warehouse. This is where that top-right color earns its keep. The week color tells you at a glance what's a live order for this week and what's a return from a previous one. Keep those two apart, and you'll never hand somebody the wrong bag.
scenes.s9: And that's a route, start to finish. Welcome to Locale.
